newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian MTBE - Gasoline drags market down.
newsitem.headline: Asian MTBE - Gasoline drags market down.

text.p: Asian methyl tertiary butyl ether (MTBE) prices extended their losses on the back of weak gasoline prices which fell to a five-month low, industry sources said on Wednesday.
"Gasoline has come off quite heavily...fob MTBE prices have slipped below $265," said one producer.
Traders assessed free-on-board (fob) Singapore MTBE lifting end-April/May at around $260-$265 per tonne, down from $260 to $270 last week.

High inventories in Singapore of gasoline and weak regional demand have depressed gasoline prices to low $24.80 per barrel for the 95-octane grade, a sharp drop from its peak of around $29.00 just over a month ago.

"Blending demand (for MTBE) has been quite minimal because there is alot of finished gasoline," a trader said. "There has been no real action in the past two weeks other than some discussions in the mandated markets such as Thailand."
Thai refiner Bangchak Petroleum Plc bought by tender 1,500-tonne of MTBE for delivery in May at around $270 per tonne c-and-f Bangkok, from Saudi Basic Industries Corp (SABIC), industry sources said.
Reflective of the softer tone of the market, the award was slightly lower than Bangchak's last purchase, for April 16-30 delivery, also from SABIC at $270-$275 c-and-f.
U.S. demand has yet to emerge as the arbitrage window has yet to open. Singapore fob prices need to fall to around $255 and the U.S. has to stay steady for the arb to work.
"It is not too far away...provided, the U.S. west coast is sucking up barrels because there are plenty of supplies from other regions," a trader said on the arbitage possibility.
On the supply side, some South Korean producers were heard offering some May cargoes.
"It depends on the price," a South Korean refiner said. "We have some availabilities but we have to check the production costs and the market price."
The South Korean refiner last week sold around 5,000 tonnes lifting in May to a western trader at $255-$260 fob Ulsan, and may still have some export availabilities.
"The current price is not so acceptable," the seller said.
